Reweight a cohort survey design

Source: R/design.R
nis_reweight.Rd

Multiplies cohort discharge survey weights by supplied propensity weights, retains the placeholder rows for hospital-years without cohort discharges, and rebuilds the nested survey design. This experimental method is intended for analysts who have validated their weighting specification against a full-data reference design.

Usage

nis_reweight(design, weights)

Arguments

design

A result of nis_design().

weights

Numeric weights aligned with the cohort rows of design, or an unquoted numeric column name in the design data. They are matched to rows by position, so take them from design$variables in that order (for example, fit the propensity model on design$variables) and do not reorder or subset the rows first.

Value

A filtered srvyr::tbl_svy survey design.

Weighted totals

The result multiplies the discharge weights by weights, so survey_total() and similar totals no longer estimate national discharge counts. Use the result for ratios, means and model estimates, and report national counts from the design before reweighting. Each call multiplies the weights again, so call nis_reweight() once on the result of nis_design(); calling it on an already reweighted design compounds the weights.

See also

Survey design and weighting.

Other survey-design: nis_design()

Examples

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")

design <- nis_design(nis, heart_failure, keep = c(AGE, FEMALE))
#> Cohort: 108 discharges; weighted N 124.8; 18 hospitals across 2 years.

# Illustrative weights only; use weights from your own validated model
reweighted <- nis_reweight(design, ifelse(AGE >= 65, 1.2, 0.9))
srvyr::summarise(reweighted, weighted_total = srvyr::survey_total())
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   weighted_total weighted_total_se
#>            <dbl>             <dbl>
#> 1           127.              17.7
